items.t: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE); hepatic coma.

src.q: 2. For the treatment of hepatic encephalopathy (HE); hepatic coma.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions stated in the UK SmPC. BNF not accessed.

items.t: Adults and adolescents: start 15-45 ml daily, maintenance 15-30 ml daily, as a single dose or two divided doses. Adjust after a few days to response; effect may take 2-3 days.

src.q: Adults and adolescents 15-45 ml, corresponding to 1-3 sachets 15-30 ml, corresponding to 1-2 sachets
Lactulose may be given as a single daily dose or in two divided doses.
Several days (2-3 days) of treatment may be needed before treatment effect occurs.

items.t: Adults: start 30-45 ml three to four times daily; adjust to a maintenance dose giving two or three soft stools each day.

src.q: Starting dose : 3 to 4 times daily 30-45 ml (6-9 x 5 ml spoonfuls) or 2-3 sachets.
This dose may be adjusted to the maintenance dose to achieve two or three soft stools each day.

items.t: Elderly, renal or hepatic impairment: no special dose recommendations (negligible systemic exposure).

src.q: Elderly patients and patients with renal or hepatic insufficiency No special dosage recommendations exist, since systemic exposure to lactulose is negligible.

items.t: Constipation: children 7-14 years start 15 ml daily, maintenance 10-15 ml daily; 1-6 years 5-10 ml daily; infants under 1 year up to 5 ml daily.

src.q: Children (7-14 years) 15 ml, corresponding to 1 sachet 10-15 ml, corresponding to 1 sachet*
Children (1-6 years) 5-10 ml 5-10 ml Infants under 1 year up to 5 ml up to 5 ml

items.t: Laxatives in children should be exceptional and under medical supervision.

src.q: Use of laxatives in children should be exceptional and under medical supervision.

items.t: Hepatic encephalopathy: safety and efficacy not established in children (newborn to 18 years).

src.q: The safety and efficacy in children (newborn to 18 years of age) with HE have not been established.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to lactulose or any excipient.

src.q: 4.3 Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substance or any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Galactosaemia.

src.q: Galactosaemia.

items.t: Gastrointestinal obstruction, perforation or risk of perforation.

src.q: Gastro-intestinal obstruction, -perforation or risk of perforation.

items.t: Evaluate painful abdominal symptoms of unknown cause before starting, to exclude perforation or obstruction.

src.q: Painful abdominal symptoms of undetermined cause should be evaluated to exclude undiagnosed perforation or obstruction

items.t: Chronic use of unadjusted doses and misuse can cause diarrhoea and electrolyte disturbance.

src.q: Chronic use of unadjusted doses and misuse can lead to diarrhoea and disturbance of the electrolyte balance.

items.t: Diabetes: constipation doses should not be a problem; the higher HE doses may need to be taken into account.

src.q: The dose normally used in constipation should not pose a problem for diabetics.
The dose used in the treatment of HE is usually much higher and may need to be taken into consideration for diabetics.

items.t: Rare hereditary galactose or fructose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption: should not take. Lactose intolerance: give with care.

src.q: patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose or fructose intolerance, the total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
Lactulose should be administered with care to patients who are intolerant to lactose.

items.t: If not effective after several days, reconsider the dose and/or other measures.

src.q: In case of insufficient therapeutic effect after several days the dose and/or additional measures should be re-considered.

interactions.note: UK SmPC 4.5: no interaction studies have been performed; no interactions listed.

items.t: No dose adjustment; systemic exposure is negligible.

src.q: Elderly patients and patients with renal or hepatic insufficiency No special dosage recommendations exist, since systemic exposure to lactulose is negligible.

items.t: Can be used in pregnancy (negligible systemic exposure).

src.q: Duphalac can be used during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS: if diet and lifestyle changes fail, a laxative can be used in pregnancy; osmotic laxatives such as lactulose are not absorbed and will not reach the baby.

src.q: If changes to lifestyle and diet have not worked to treat constipation, a laxative can be taken in pregnancy if recommended by a pharmacist, midwife, or doctor.
They are not absorbed into the body and therefore will not reach the baby.

items.t: Can be used during breastfeeding.

src.q: Duphalac can be used during breast-feeding.

items.t: SPS: can be used during breastfeeding; as a precaution monitor the infant for diarrhoea, vomiting or irritability.

src.q: Lactulose can be used during breastfeeding.
As a precaution monitor the infant for diarrhoea, vomiting or irritability.

items.t: No effects on fertility expected (negligible systemic exposure).

src.q: Fertility No effects are to be expected, since systemic exposure to lactulose is negligible.

items.t: Very common: diarrhoea. Common: flatulence, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting.

src.q: Gastrointestinal disorders Diarrhoea Flatulence, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting

items.t: Flatulence in the first few days usually settles after a couple of days.

src.q: Flatulence may occur during the first few days of treatment. As a rule it disappears after a couple of days.

items.t: Abdominal pain and diarrhoea at higher than instructed doses: reduce the dose.

src.q: When dosages higher than instructed are used, abdominal pain and diarrhoea may occur. In such a case the dosage should be decreased.

items.t: Long-term high doses (usually in HE) can cause electrolyte imbalance from diarrhoea: adjust dose to two or three formed stools per day.

src.q: If high doses (normally only associated with hepatic encephalopathy, HE) are used for an extended period of time, the patient may experience an electrolyte imbalance due to diarrhoea.
Dosage should then be adjusted to obtain two or three formed stools per day.

items.t: Hypersensitivity reactions (rash, pruritus, urticaria) reported (frequency not known).

src.q: Immune system disorders Hypersensitvity reactions

items.t: Long-term high-dose use: watch for diarrhoea and electrolyte imbalance; adjust dose to two or three formed stools per day.

src.q: Dosage should then be adjusted to obtain two or three formed stools per day.

items.t: Can be taken diluted or undiluted, with water or fruit juice. Swallow each dose at once; do not keep it in the mouth.

src.q: Each dose may if necessary be taken with water or fruit juices, etc.
Each dose of lactulose should be swallowed in one and should not be kept in the mouth for an extended period of time.

items.t: Single daily dose: take at the same time each day, e.g. at breakfast.

src.q: In case of single daily dose, this should be taken at the same time, e.g. during breakfast.

items.t: Drink enough fluid (1.5-2 litres a day) while taking laxatives.

src.q: During the therapy with laxatives it is recommended to drink sufficient amounts of fluids (1.5-2 litres, equal to 6-8 glasses) during the day.

items.t: It can take 2-3 days to work.

src.q: Several days (2-3 days) of treatment may be needed before treatment effect occurs.
